subject: British West Indies anti-resistance fiscal law and Topsham Dragon slave ship revolt

jamaica_1699_law.title: An Act for raising Parties to Suppress Rebellious and Runaway Negroes
jamaica_1699_law.source_repository: University of New Brunswick, Laws of Enslavement and Freedom in the Anglo-Atlantic World
jamaica_1699_law.underlying_print: The Laws of Jamaica, printed in London by W. Wilkins, 1716, pp.257–261
jamaica_1699_law.reason_exact_day_unknown: University law database explicitly records an inexact historical date; 1699-01-01 is a database stand-in, not proven enactment day
jamaica_1699_law.payer: colonial Jamaica public revenue; warrant via governor and council
jamaica_1699_law.decree_vs_actual_spending: statutory authorised rates only, not audited actual payments or number of military expeditions
jamaica_1699_law.wording_note: Original statute transcribed describes earlier conditional wartime emancipations against French, and subsequent compensation to previous enslavers; payments are not emancipation compensation to named formerly enslaved individuals. Do not infer sale price, employer profits, or person's intrinsic value from this legislated transfer.
jamaica_1699_law.mapped_location: Jamaica general law only, no raid or battlefield site

dragon_1699.temporal_precision: 1699 voyage, precise revolt day not verified
dragon_1699.resistance_type: Shipboard revolt while at African coast
dragon_1699.quoted_museum: PortCities Bristol / Bristol's Museums, The south west ports of England
dragon_1699.shipowners_grouped_separately: Six owners from Topsham, Bristol Museum description
dragon_1699.business_loss_category: Museum estimates owner-side cargo value at historical £400; no audited investment profit; Museum historical present-value equivalence intentionally omitted
dragon_1699.source_level: institutional museum secondary publication, original ship log / Tattersfield 1991 chapters not directly viewed
dragon_1699.uncertainty: Merchant-port study elsewhere names captain Christopher Butcher; Taylor 2006 secondary chronology names Henry Taylor for the same alleged Dragon revolt. This is an unresolved captain identity conflict; do not merge with other ships or invent battlefield coordinates.

general_limitations: The statutory monthly pay was an incentive, not evidence any given group was actually hunted in a precise mapped district on that date.
The Dragon was a ship with a reported uprising outside the 2019/2020 14-coded British sample; an omission from the snapshot is not evidence the revolt did not occur.
No percentages inferred from museum's £400 value or 14 remaining; do not add 1699 Dragon to database RESISTANCE=1 observed count.
UNB edition contains 1716 printing of the 1699 enacted text; distinct bibliography levels.
